content: Cresol Red, also known by its full chemical name o-Cresolsulfonephthalein, is a triarylmethane dye that is commonly utilized for pH monitoring in aquaria. This compound can serve as a substitute for water in various molecular reactions, such as restriction digestion or polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Additionally, Cresol Red functions as a color marker to track the progress of agarose gel electrophoresis and polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis. In a 1% agarose gel, Cresol Red migrates at a rate approximately equivalent to a DNA molecule of 125 base pairs (bp) in size, although this migration rate can vary depending on the concentration of the buffer and other components in the system. Other dyes, such as Bromophenol Blue and Xylene Cyanol, can also be employed for similar purposes.
